page: Amazon Web Services r8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server configuration powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton architecture. The instance runs on an arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor at 2.8 GHz, supplying 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core. The hardware profile is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core allocation. The CPU features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It features no local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, relying on remote block storage and a 15 Gbps baseline network link.

Performance benchmarks show exceptional throughput across memory-dependent subsystems. The instance reaches top-tier memory bandwidth metrics, recording 402.49 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 183.47 GB/sec in write transfers. Synthetic database assessments place the server in the top decile with a PassMark database score of 47,337.28, complemented by 66.65 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Multi-threaded processing remains strong, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,614.0. In contrast, single-core compute performance falls within the middle tiers, and LLM text generation benchmarks exhibit lower throughput.

The absence of onboard storage and graphics acceleration directs cost efficiency entirely toward system memory capacity and CPU core parallelism. The dedicated physical core structure avoids hyperthreading contention, delivering predictable execution for dense, concurrent processes. Consequently, the r8g.8xlarge is positioned specifically for high-capacity in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, caching clusters, large-scale relational database engines, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server built on the 64-bit ARM AWS Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Network connectivity operates at a 15 Gbps baseline, with no onboard local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance achieves top-tier results in uncached memory read bandwidth at 402.49 GB/sec, uncached write bandwidth at 183.47 GB/sec, and database operations scoring 47,337.28. It also yields 66.65 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,614.0. Single-core performance and large language model inference remain in average tiers. The system provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, particularly in-memory caching, distributed key-value stores, and relational database hosting.
